name: Shillong
description: Capital of Meghalaya and headquarters of East Khasi Hills, known as the Scotland of the East. A popular hill station at about 1,500 m elevation with pine forests, colonial architecture, markets, and access to waterfalls and viewpoints.
facts: Capital and HQ of East Khasi Hills
Named after the deity Lei Shyllong

name: Shillong Peak
description: Highest point in Meghalaya at about 1,966 m, offering panoramic views of Shillong city and surrounding hills. Site of the sacred Lei Shillong shrine; popular for sunsets and photography.
facts: Sacred to Khasi as abode of Lei Shillong
Popular for panoramic views and sunsets

name: Elephant Falls
description: Three-tier waterfall near Upper Shillong, locally known as Ka Kshaid Lai Pateng Khohsiew. Cascades over fern-covered rocks; easily accessible from the Shillong-Cherrapunji road.
facts: Named after a former elephant-shaped rock

name: Ward's Lake
description: Man-made lake in the heart of Shillong, named after Sir William Ward. Features a walking path, gardens, and boating; a central recreational spot in the city.
facts: Named after Chief Commissioner Sir William Ward

name: Sohra (Cherrapunji)
description: Subdivisional town on the southern slopes of the Khasi Hills, one of the wettest places on Earth. Gateway to numerous waterfalls, caves, living root bridges, and viewpoints over deep gorges.
facts: Receives among the highest rainfall globally
Base for Nohkalikai and living root bridges

name: Nohkalikai Falls
description: Tallest plunge waterfall in India at about 340 m, plunging from the Cherrapunji plateau into a green pool. Fed by monsoon rains; one of the most iconic sights near Sohra.
facts: Best viewed in monsoon for full flow

name: Nohsngithiang Falls (Seven Sisters Falls)
description: Series of seven cascading streams near Mawsmai, dropping dramatically over a cliff. One of the tallest waterfalls in India; spectacular during monsoon.

name: Mawsmai Cave
description: Limestone cave near Sohra with illuminated passages and formations. One of the more accessible caves in the region, popular with visitors exploring the Cherrapunji circuit.

name: Double Decker Living Root Bridge (Nongriat)
description: Unique two-tier living root bridge in Nongriat village, grown from Ficus elastica roots by Khasi communities over generations. Accessible via a steep trek of thousands of steps from Tyrna; a highlight of Meghalaya's bio-engineering.
facts: In Nongriat village, East Khasi Hills
About 15 km from Sohra via Tyrna
Two stacked root bridges spanning a stream

name: Mawlynnong Village
description: Widely known as Asia's cleanest village, a Khasi settlement near the Bangladesh border with neat gardens, bamboo dustbins, and living root bridges nearby. Promotes community-led eco-tourism and cleanliness.
facts: Community-managed tourism and living root bridges

name: Laitlum Canyon
description: Dramatic cliff-top viewpoint about 25 km from Shillong overlooking deep green canyons and valleys. Known for sunrise/sunset views and a steep path down to the valley floor.
facts: Steep stairs to Rasong village below

name: Mawphlang Sacred Forest
description: Ancient sacred grove protected by Khasi tradition where nothing may be removed. Features old-growth forest, monoliths, and guided walks; a key cultural and biodiversity site about 25 km from Shillong.
facts: Guided walks only; nothing may be taken out
